established.fact: VS `[[stage_in]]` attribute fetch is IN-SHADER SOFTWARE FETCH. There is no fixed-function attribute-fetch descriptor: stride/offset/format live in the compiled shader; the command-stream attribute table at gpu_va 0x10000100000 supplies only the base pointer, preloaded into a uniform slot selected by `device_load` byte+4 `base_slot = 0x03`.

No two-run gate (2026-07-07, predates that regime).

established.fact: Every tested vertex-format category produces mutually distinct compiled VS bytes from the same attribute slot, and every layout knob independently moves the compiled bytes. established.fact: Per-stage ENTRY contract: nothing is preloaded into a GPR at entry, in any stage. Compute must emit `get_sr` for thread IDs; vertex must emit `get_sr` for vertex_id/instance_id; fragment gets varyings only through the interpolation datapath and position/front_facing through `get_sr`. Only the UNIFORM register file is preloaded (buffer base pointers + scalar constant uniforms), populated by the constant/uniform program.

2_outputs.scope: FS outputs: color, MRT, dual source, depth, stencil, sample mask, discard/demote, and side-effect order. VS pre-raster outputs.
2_outputs.coverage_verdict: The STRONGEST sub-area. Field-level legal-value maps exist ON G17P for the whole fragment output path; the behavioural/semantic layer is M4-only.

established.fact: The fragment output path is emittable field-by-field on G17P: `frag_tile_setup` -> `frag_color_pack` -> `frag_color_store` / `imageblock_store`, plus `frag_depth_store`. Named silent-zero traps: `frag_color_store.mask` bit 0 clear gives a SILENT ZERO; `frag_color_pack.src_desc` off `mod 8 in {4,6}` silently zeroes; `imageblock_store.b6` bit 0 clear silently zeroes; `frag_depth_store.b4` is correct ONLY at 0 and silently zeroes at every other residue mod 32.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 99,526 swept cases over 2 gated runs; each named field swept densely over its full 8-bit range unless a hang budget stopped it (19 of 105 promoted fields are `isolated-byte-diff` for that reason, each recording its exact swept count). 232 exact machine-checked bit rules over 244 comparable (arm, field) triples.

established.fact: `frag_tile_setup` has only ONE live field. `sel`, `access` and `b5` are inert over all 256 values on 5-8 structurally different carriers; only `b1` is live (silent_zero iff mod 8 <= 1).
established.label: HW-VALIDATED measurement, labelled `single-template-inference` for emitter purposes
established.tested_range: 256 values x 8 arms (EXP-0163), on carriers ibmrt/layer/mrt3/tileread/tilerw2. EXP-0163 is PROVISIONAL: ONE gated run; run02 was deferred behind a coordinated quiet window.
established.caveat: EXP-0163 deliberately labels these INERT-ROBUST negatives `single-template-inference`, not `hardware-run`, because its own emitter guidance is 'emit the compiler-observed value' - a dependency on a captured template, which closure rule 1 forbids.

established.fact: A fragment colour-store VARIANT that db.json does not decode: `byte+1 == 0x86` (vs 0x06 plain and 0x16 first-after-tile-setup). It falls through to a 14-byte COMPUTE `device_store` in a fragment program that has no writable device buffer. Consequence: every occurrence census ever run against the `frag_color_store` descriptor is unquantified over this form.
established.artifact: experiments/EXP-0163-g17p-inert-liveness/RESULTS.md sec.4b; carrier kernels/k_texcube.metal, store at offset 188

established.tested_range: One carrier (k_texcube: four texture samples of a 2D, 3D, cube and 2D-array texture then a float4 return into RGBA32Float). byte+1 was NEVER swept, so the nibble split is a proposal, not a validated fix.

established.fact: `frag_color_store` semantics: byte+1 == 0x06 is the FRAGMENT tile-store variant (the compute device store is 0x00, 14 B); byte+3 is the source colour GPR; byte+5 is the render-target index as (rt<<1) - RT0=0x00, RT1=0x02, RT2=0x04. Splicing byte+5 0x00->0x02 (store to an absent RT1) leaves RT0 at the clear colour; corrupting byte+1 0x06->0x00 also leaves RT0 clear. MRT emits one store per target, each in its own 0x87/0x07 tile bracket.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED (splice-and-observe)
established.tested_range: 27 authored kernels; 36 hex dumps; 6 numbered validation sections. No run count, no cross-run gate (2026-07-07).

established.fact: MRT scales cleanly and independently. Attachment count 1..8 all render correctly with independently-addressed, independently-correct per-target values; adding targets does not perturb lower-indexed ones. The hard ceiling is EXACTLY 8: index 8 raises a FATAL, UNCATCHABLE process abort the instant the attachment array is indexed (`attachmentIndex(8) must be < 8`), with no pipeline or shader involved.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: natt = 1..8 spot-checked at 1 and 8 to exact half-float match; API index probe at 0, 7, 8, 9. 148/148 cases byte-identical across 2 gated runs.

established.fact: Dual-source blend is native and the naive model is WRONG. `Source1Color`/`Source1Alpha` are FACTOR choices that pull index(1)'s value in as a coefficient; they do not replace index(0) as the multiplicand. The confirmed equation is `result = src0 * factor(src1) + dst * dstFactor`. At the ISA level dual source is 'just an extra output register + one store (no distinct op)'.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED (M4 equation) + OWN-SHADER-DIFF (G17P ISA shape)
established.target: M4 / G16G for the equation; A18 Pro / G17P for the ISA shape
established.tested_range: c0*c1 vs c0*c0 discriminated to 3 decimal places; the discriminating probe (sourceRGBBlendFactor=SourceColor) is a DISCLOSED single-run non-frozen supplementary probe, outside the two-run gate.

established.fact: Explicit fragment depth output genuinely overrides the interpolated rasterizer depth for all three MSL qualifiers under a compare function that cannot mask the write. Shader-supplied `[[depth(any)]]` output is LATE, not early.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 4 depth cases exact, both runs; probe z held at a constant 0.0 so any other buffer value is unambiguous. `[[early_fragment_tests]]` gives ran=0/32 in the fail region vs 32/32 for ordinary and shader-depth testing.

established.fact: `[[stencil]]` is a real MSL fragment output and its value overrides the encode-time `stencilReferenceValue` under MTLStencilOperationReplace. Values beyond 255 TRUNCATE to their low 8 bits (`value & 0xFF`), they do NOT clamp. `int` (signed) is rejected at compile time; a driver must materialize the value as `uint`/`ushort`.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: uint 0,1,127,254,255,256,257,511,65535,4294967295; ushort 300,255. 256 and 257 are the DECISIVE disambiguators (low byte != 255) and both match truncation, refuting clamp-to-255. 12/12 exact, both runs.

established.fact: A dedicated kill / target-mask instruction EXISTS and is not folded into any store: a 6-byte submission op `57 <B1> 54 <B3> <B4> <B5>` immediately followed by a 6-byte companion `07 02 54 01 <B4'> <B5'>`. It is emitted iff the shader calls `discard_fragment()` or writes `[[sample_mask]]`, never for an unrelated divergent branch. Its byte+4 bits[4:0] are a source-register select, splice-proven: value 0x00 reads the real mask; 0x01/0x02/0x04/0x08/0x10 read an always-zero register and kill the fragment on color, depth AND occlusion together.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED for byte+4; STRUCTURAL/UNKNOWN for the rest of the bit decode
established.tested_range: 9 differential-compile localization probes; byte+4 swept over {0x00,0x01,0x02,0x04,0x08,0x10,0x20,0x40,0x80,0xFE,0xFF}; null splices on own byte+1/+3/+5 and companion byte+3/+4/+5 recorded. 78/78 cases byte-identical across 2 gated runs. B1 takes exactly two values, 0x1c (compile-time-provable unconditional) and 0x14 (everything else).

established.fact: The same `0x57` opcode is SHARED between the vertex varying store and this fragment kill op, and the discriminator is byte+1's low three bits, NOT byte+2. On G17P: `byte+1 & 7 == 6` preserves the 8-byte VERTEX varying store; `== 4` or `== 5` preserves the 6-byte FRAGMENT kill/target-mask op; `== 3` or `== 7` FAULTS in the vertex form; `== 0,1,2` SILENTLY ZERO. byte+2 is a DON'T-CARE across all 256 values on four independent programs, so the `byte+2 == 0x54` the current descriptor leans on selects nothing.
established.experiment: EXP-0155-g17p-emit-tex-frag sec.4.1 (resolving the collision EXP-0091 first reported)
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: byte+2: all 256 values on 4 programs (6-byte fragment form c_kill/c_mask and 8-byte vertex form c_iter/c_vary16). byte+1: two independent code paths (the 0x57 collision probe and the `vary_store.hint1` field sweep) produce the identical residue rule.
established.note: This is the one place where an M4 finding (EXP-0091) was followed through to a direct G17P resolution.

established.fact: The slot an emitter must get right is `vary_store.out_slot`, NOT `vary_slot.slot`. `vary_slot.sel` (byte+1) leaves the pixel unchanged for exactly one value (0x0c) and moves it for all 255 others, while `vary_slot.slot` (byte+3) was inert across all 256 values on two different vertex programs. EXP-0172 then confirmed the positive half on hardware: `slot` IS live, but it is EXACTLY BIT 2 - all 128 values with bit 2 set move the observation and all 128 with it clear do not, with no exceptions in either run - and bit 2 is NOT where the compiler puts the index (its own baselines are 0x00/0x20/0x40, the varying index shifted left by 5).
established.label: HW-VALIDATED (`hardware-run`)
established.tested_range: EXP-0155: 256 values on two vertex programs (c_iter with 4 varyings, c_vary16 with 12). EXP-0172: 256 values x 4 arms x 2 gated runs, 100% per-value cross-run agreement on the one arm (vsrc) with strict detection power; the other three arms (vmany, vhalf, vflat) had no detection power and moved at 0 of 256.
established.note: EXP-0172's own verdict note: 'it is a lever, but not the one an implementer wants' (DEF-0172-3).

established.fact: `[[sample_mask]]`'s effective width is EXACTLY the configured sample count: the mask is the low N bits and every bit at position >= N is silently, uniformly inert - no aliasing, no wraparound, no fault, even at 0xFFFFFFFF. A driver may emit a naive all-ones mask for any legal N.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED

established.fact: Fragment discard has SPIR-V DEMOTE semantics (`discard_is_demote = true`): a discarded lane keeps executing, and its post-discard mutation reaches a surviving neighbour through `fwidth` (exactly 999.0 vs 1.0 control), through `quad_shuffle_xor` (the demoted lane's live post-discard register value), and through an implicit-LOD sample's shared quad derivative.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 3 paired demote probes (fwidth before/after, quad_shuffle, implicit-LOD texture) each with its own control, 78/78 byte-identical across 2 runs.

established.fact: Side-effect suppression for a demoted lane is INHERENT and complete across five channels - colour, depth, device-buffer store, global atomic, AND `[[sample_mask]]` write - all moving together deterministically for every suppressed lane.
established.experiment: EXP-0091-m4-fragment-sample-discard (GLFS-A06, 4 channels) + EXP-0111-m4-fragment-semantics (FS-12, the sample-mask channel)
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 16/16 control lanes written vs 8/16 test lanes suppressed; atomic counter 8 vs 16; poisoned slot stays 0xEEEEEEEE. FS-12 at N=4: discarded pixel resolves to exactly 0.0.

established.fact: Output ORDERING: source-statement order of colour/depth/stencil struct-field computation is provably irrelevant (two functions computing identical values in opposite source order compile byte-identically). A real depth-test failure driven by the shader's own depth output completely suppresses colour AND stencil writes, and the stencil op that fires is exactly the one configured for that outcome - verified in BOTH op-assignment directions.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 2 source orders (structural byte-identity + functional identity); 2 stencil-op assignments x 2 sides (pass/fail), both runs byte-identical.

established.fact: A per-fragment DIVERGENT render-target selection works, but its encoding is not understood: the compiled program contains only ONE `frag_color_store` with `rt_index = 0` (an immediate), preceded by `icmp_pred`+`sel`, and TWO `frag_tile_setup` brackets with selector bytes 0x0 and 0xc - which does not match EXP-0029's 0x0/0x4/0x8 fixed-RT-index table for ordinary static MRT. Hardware readback nevertheless proves correct independent routing to 2 and to 3 distinct targets.
established.label: PARTIAL / UNKNOWN mechanism (readback is HW-VALIDATED; the encoding is not explained)
established.tested_range: 2-way and 3-way divergence, exact per-pixel readback 2/2 and 3/3. An array-typed fragment-output struct is REJECTED at compile time ('invalid return type ... for fragment function').

established.fact: VS pre-raster special outputs, boundary behaviour: NaN in any position component discards the primitive; +Inf x or y discards while -Inf x or y produces a full fill; w = +0.0 and w = -0.0 behave identically. `[[point_size]]` is exact for 4..511 and CLAMPS 512, 513, 1000, 1e8, NaN and +Inf to the identical 511x511 footprint (ceiling confirmed independent of target size at 2000x2000); 0 and every negative-Inf value discards, while mid-negative values give anomalous off-centre squares that were recorded, not explained. `[[render_target_array_index]]` and `[[viewport_array_index]]` CLAMP every out-of-range value to exactly index 0 - not to N-1, not modulo, not discard.

established.tested_range: position_special 14 cases on a 4x4 target; point_size 20 cases on 600x600 (re-tested at 2000x2000); layer_oob 13 cases at N=4 and N=8; viewport_oob 8 cases at N=4. 140/140 cases byte-identical across 2 gated runs, zero CMDBUF_ERROR.

established.fact: Provoking vertex is FIXED to the first-fetched vertex of each assembled primitive (the D3D/Vulkan FIRST_VERTEX convention), per primitive, and Metal exposes no API to change it. A driver targeting GL's default LAST_VERTEX convention must emulate it (index rewrite / attribute duplication).
established.label: HW-VALIDATED (behaviour) + PUBLIC-negative (the API-absence half is explicitly 'a documented negative, not a proof of absence across the entire framework')
established.tested_range: 3 cases: direct list -> vertex 0's colour; indices [2,1,0] -> vertex 2's colour (so it tracks which vertex was FETCHED first, not vertex_id==0); triangle strip -> second triangle takes vertex 1, its own first window vertex, NOT the newest vertex 3.
established.supersedes: EXP-0029 (G17P) said only 'flat shading takes vertex 0's value'; EXP-0097 explicitly rules out that reading.

3_sysvals.scope: FS and CS system values, their get_sr selectors, and their delivery path.
3_sysvals.coverage_verdict: GOOD on M4/G16G. On G17P the SELECTOR ITSELF is not emitter-grade: `get_sr.sr_sel` is labelled `untested`, so no system value can be emitted with confidence on the documentation target.

established.fact: The `get_sr` SR number is BYTE1 (bits [8:16]), correcting EXP-0010 which called byte0's high nibble the selector - that nibble is the DESTINATION GPR. byte0 bit 3 is a form/width modifier that does NOT change which SR is read.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED (splice)
established.tested_range: SR bytes {0x82, 0x85, 0x98, 0x9c, 0xa0, 0xa4} spliced on `hw_tidx` at grid=64/tg=64, all exact matches. No cross-run gate.

established.fact: `sr_sel` bit 7 is a structural discriminator over the FULL 256-value space. 0x80-0xFF reads the special-register file (16 named exactly, ~106 aliasing a known SR's pattern, 4 unclassified constants, 2 unclassified period-4 patterns). 0x00-0x7F instead materializes the SELECTOR BYTE ITSELF into the destination at a single fixed slot - an exact linear identity for all 128 values. No value in 0x00-0xFF raises a command-buffer error: the field has NO fault mode.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: Exhaustive 0x00-0xFF (256 cases) x 2 gated runs, byte-identical. The MECHANISM behind the single-slot materialization is recorded UNKNOWN, not asserted.

established.fact: The GPR file's hard ceiling is EXACTLY 96 along the get_sr-dst / device_store-index_reg addressing path: registers 0..95 round-trip exactly; 96, 97, 100, 111, 120, 127 all fault (CMDBUF_ERROR / GPU Hang) deterministically; register 112 is GENUINELY NONDETERMINISTIC (5 faults / 3 silent all-zero successes over 8 informal repeats plus a run01/run02 split). There is no wraparound scheme.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED for the 0-95/96-127 boundary; PARTIAL within 96-127
established.tested_range: 23 register points, not exhaustive over 0..127. The formal `verify.py --captured` cross-run gate DOES NOT PASS for the full 300-case set because of reg_112; this is reported rather than force-closed.
established.g17p_corroboration: EXP-0155 independently reproduced the same GPR>=96 boundary on G17P across 7 different fields (iter.dst, iter_at.dst, frag_color_pack.dst, simd_ballot.dst, simd_reduce.dst, simd_shuffle.dst, imageblock_store.src): (value & 0xC0) == 0xC0 with bit1 clear FAULTS, with bit1 set HANGS. Core count is throughput, not register file.

established.fact: SR 0x88 = base_vertex and 0x8a = base_instance, UPGRADED from `(inferred)` to HW-VALIDATED. `vertex_id` and `instance_id` are base-inclusive and wrap mod 2^32; base_vertex reads back as the unsigned reinterpretation of a negative host value.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 9 cases: baseVertex 0/100/1000000/-5/-1/INT32_MAX, baseInstance 0/50/500000/UINT32_MAX with instanceCount 2 for the wrap. All 9 exact, both runs byte-identical.
established.note: EXP-0031 (G17P) had assigned 0x88/0x8a by byte-diff on a NON-INDEXED, ZERO-BASE draw - indistinguishable from 'always reads zero'. The G17P side of this fact remains that weak byte-diff.

established.fact: `threadgroups_per_grid` (the load_num_workgroups lowering) reports exactly the requested count for direct dispatch and exactly the raw record for indirect dispatch, with no clamp, truncation or fault at any tested value including UINT32_MAX on one axis and a 65535x65535 product. A bare `get_sr 0xa8` returns threads_per_threadgroup.x, NOT the workgroup count - the real lowering is get_sr 0xa8/a9/aa + a device_load + a divide.
established.experiment: EXP-0092-m4-sysval-abi (GLIO-A05), re-confirming RT-7's A18 finding on M4
established.label: HW-VALIDATED for the numeric pass-through
established.tested_range: 12 cases (6 direct, 6 indirect), both runs byte-identical. A zero on ANY axis means no invocation runs, so `indirect_all_zero` / `indirect_zero_x` are OBSERVED_NO_ORACLE, not confirmation of a (0,0,0) read.

established.fact: Fragment `get_sr` selectors: 0xa0 = integer pixel X and 0xa1 = integer pixel Y (splice-validated IN THE FRAGMENT STAGE by a mutual swap on a single-pixel triangle); 0xc5 = front_facing, HW-validated on both windings; 0x84 = helper-thread status. `point_coord` and `barycentric_coord` are INTERPOLATED (the 0x2f family), not get_sr; `primitive_id` is a flat tiler-output load. The SR namespace is stage-contextual - 0xa0/0xa1 mean 'position x/y for the running stage'.
established.experiment: EXP-0031-sr-abi (table, G17P) + EXP-0111-m4-fragment-semantics FS-01 (the 0xa0/0xa1 splice, M4) + EXP-0091 GLFS-A03 (0x84)
established.label: 0xc5 HW-VALIDATED on G17P; 0xa0/0xa1 INFERRED on G17P (byte-diff) and HW-VALIDATED on M4; 0x84 named but its raw bit pattern explicitly NOT validated
established.tested_range: EXP-0111: single-pixel triangle at (2,1) of a 3x2 target; baseline (2.5,1.5); 0xa0->0xa1 gives (1.5,1.5); 0xa1->0xa0 gives (2.5,2.5). A clean mutual swap. 56/56 cases byte-identical across 2 gated runs.
established.note: The compiler emits `cvt_i2f` on the get_sr result, so the SR delivers a RAW INTEGER; the +0.5 pixel-centre offset is the language's, not the hardware's.

established.fact: System values are NOT preloaded into uniform registers. Reading vertex_id/instance_id changes ONLY the shader code; the USC uniform preamble is byte-identical (0 words). What the preamble does preload is buffer/vertex base pointers and scalar constant uniforms.
established.label: DATA-TRACE-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 34 draws, all status=4, 0 faults. Change-one-Metal-parameter byte-diffing of our own control BOs. No cross-run gate (2026-07-07).

not_established: `get_sr.sr_sel` is `untested` on G17P in tools/agx-isa/validation.json (EXP-0169, 256 dense values but only ONE carrier). `dp_width` and `dp_marker` are likewise `untested`. So `get_sr` is NOT emittable and no system value can be emitted on the documentation target.

established.fact: Perspective correction is a MULTI-INSTRUCTION LOWERING, not a mode bit: linear/no-perspective is four `iter` with byte+6==0x00; perspective ADDS a W-denominator `iter` (byte+6==0x04), an `0xaf` reciprocal, and a per-component multiply. `iter` is 10 bytes (byte0 0x2f/0xaf, byte+2==0x54), one op per interpolated component; byte+5 is the source varying-slot as (slot<<1) and byte+6 is the mode. `iter_flat` is 6 bytes (byte0 0x1f) and loads the provoking-vertex attribute with no interpolation. 6_calls.scope: Prolog/main/epilog calls and branches, calling convention, register allocation across a call.
6_calls.coverage_verdict: The SEMANTIC layer is good and partly on G17P. The EMISSION layer is not: `call` is not emittable and 4 of its 5 fields are `tokenization-only` - framing only, no value semantics.

established.fact: G17P has a real CALL/RETURN implemented in the CONTROL-FLOW family (byte0 low nibble 0xf), not a dedicated opcode group. CALL is `0f 05 54 1a 8f 00 56 <off40> 00` (14 B) and the target is EXACTLY (call_instruction_address + 4) + off40. RETURN is `8f <linkmode> 54 00` (4 B) with NO TARGET FIELD - the return address comes from a hardware link register / control-flow stack. Every out-of-line call is preceded by a 4-byte call-site/frame marker `43 00 00 01` and followed by a 6-byte reconverge `0f 06 04 02 00 00`; the call reuses the 0f 05 / 0f 06 execution-mask push/pop machinery.
established.label: HW-VALIDATED for the opcode, target formula and return; the byte 0x43 marker is 'byte-observed'
established.tested_range: 4 call sites at distinct distances (-104, -158, -552, -458), helper always at section offset 64. 3 levels of nesting. NO RUN COUNT and NO CROSS-RUN GATE - this experiment predates that regime.
established.correction_it_carries: byte0 0x43 is the call/frame marker, correcting EXP-0030's claim that it was mesh-unique.

established.fact: Calling convention: arguments pass in consecutive 32-bit GPRs from r10 (arg0->r10, arg1->r11, ...); `half` args use the low 16 bits of their GPR; the return value comes back in r10 for float/int/half. For the arg counts tested there is no separate argument stack. The STACK FRAME IS THE PER-THREAD SCRATCH: a callee exceeding the 96-GPR file spills there, and a non-leaf callee also saves its link register there around inner calls.

8_linking.scope: Prolog/main/epilog live-ins/outs, calls/branches, register allocation, and resource merging across a split.
8_linking.coverage_verdict: The CONTRACT IS SPECIFIED and constructed - on M4 only - and it rests on a CALL instruction that is not emittable. This is the sub-area with the widest gap between 'we know what to do' and 'we can emit it'.

established.fact: There is NO native fixed-function or separately-loaded prolog/epilog unit. Metal's own compiler never produces a separately-addressed 'prolog' object for attribute fetch or an 'epilog' object for fragment output: every render/compute pipeline reports exactly [_agc.main.constant_program, _agc.main]. A Mesa-style prolog/epilog key-based variant split is a SOFTWARE organization choice, not something the Apple9 hardware ABI requires or exposes.

9_sideband.scope: The pipeline-wide state that links stages: USC binding grammar, UVS slot linkage, varying budget, and the fixed-function words that must agree with the shader.

established.fact: There is NO G13-style single tagged 'USC control-word list'. Binding is split across three structures: (1) textures + samplers into a Tier-2 argument buffer with a 2-pointer header [texture-array VA][sampler-array VA] followed by 32-byte texture descriptors then 8-byte sampler descriptors, where the header itself is the count/split field (num_textures = (samp_ptr - tex_ptr)/0x20); (2) buffers into a table of 8-byte LE GPU VAs in binding-index order; (3) uniform preload into a per-stage USC uniform-preamble program led by tagged 8-byte words - 0x0088_00XX register/shader-config with XX = stage x 0x0c, 0x0042_XXXX uniform-data pointer, 0x0020_00XX uniform-slot count (+2 per preloaded resource).
established.label: DATA-TRACE-VALIDATED
established.tested_range: 34 draws, all status=4, 0 faults, change-one-resource-type byte-diffing from a byte-identical baseline. No cross-run gate.

established.fact: VS->FS UVS linkage is POSITIONAL and cross-stage-compacted: `[[position]]` occupies slots 0-3 and user varyings start at slot 4, one slot per scalar component in declaration order; the FS `iter` reads them by coefficient index; only varyings the FS actually consumes are emitted. HW-validated by reorder: an identical FS reading the middle UVS slot rendered 0.200 vs 0.302 depending only on which value the VS wrote there.

established.tested_range: linkA/linkB/vary3 kernels; no cross-run gate.

established.fact: The varying budget is EXACTLY 124 user scalar components consumed by the fragment function - per scalar, independent of declared vector width and of bit width (half vs float), and counted on POST-LINK LIVENESS, never on the raw declared struct size. N=125 gives a clean pipeline rejection naming the limit; N>=127 crashes Metal's out-of-process compiler service (XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED). Clip distance is an INDEPENDENT budget of exactly 8 that is never shared with or counted against the varying budget. `cull_distance` is not a recognized MSL attribute at all and therefore consumes no budget.

established.fact: THE SYNTHESIS RULE an epilog generator must implement, read directly off Metal's own compiler: classify the configured (sourceFactor, destinationFactor, op) triple at pipeline-build time and emit `tile_read` ONLY IF the destination's true numeric value is required. Structurally confirmed: blending disabled and blending enabled with src=One/dst=Zero compile to LITERALLY THE SAME 56 bytes; src=Zero/dst=One (a dst-identity) compiles to a 16-byte stub with only a frag_tile_setup + fence and no store at all; only a genuinely data-dependent configuration is longer and contains tile_read. established.fact: LOGIC OPS - a Vulkan VK_LOGIC_OP_* capability the fixed-function-shaped Metal blend descriptor cannot express at all - were INDEPENDENTLY CONSTRUCTED as a programmable epilog and are bit-exact. clean_room_boundaries._definition: A question that can only be answered by inspecting Apple's own shaders or binaries is a BOUNDARY, not a gap. It is recorded as out of scope with its reason, exactly as EXP-0134 did for the compression codec and SFU-04.

boundaries.question: What Apple's own BG / EOT / partial-BG / partial-EOT programs contain.
boundaries.why_out_of_scope: Those are Apple-authored precompiled shaders. CLAUDE.md forbids inspecting them and forbids committing them. EXP-0108 searched for a program RECORD at the userspace<->kernel data boundary - which is lawful DATA-TRACE - and found none; it explicitly did not and must not read any Apple-authored program bytes. EXP-0108's own framing: if such a program exists, 'the Linux driver's equivalent, if it needs one at all, is likely to be its OWN synthesized routine consuming these same descriptor fields directly, rather than a reverse-engineered copy of an Apple-authored one'.
boundaries.consequence_for_the_driver: The BG/EOT program must be CONSTRUCTED, and EXP-0130 shows it can be: a tilebuffer-read / ALU / attachment-write core built from our own MSL is behaviourally exact. What stays unknown is the surrounding usc/rsrc_spec registration, which is a P0.4/P0.5 problem, not an ABI one.

boundaries.question: The scratch / helper-program protocol's binary, cfg and data field values.
boundaries.why_out_of_scope_partially: Not a clean-room boundary in the forbidden-source sense, but a HOST-OBSERVABILITY boundary that behaves like one. Three independent lawful methods (EXP-0041, EXP-0107, EXP-0125) reach the same negative; EXP-0125's conclusion is that 'the scratch/helper mechanism is not observable from userspace's own IOKit resource-map boundary on macOS'. Going further would mean reading Apple's kernel/firmware code, which is forbidden outright.
boundaries.consequence_for_the_driver: EXP-0125: the helper program and scratch-pool layout 'most likely need to be constructed from first principles against the hardware's actual behavior ... not decoded from a macOS capture'. EXP-0041's safe fallback stands: reject or avoid shaders and preambles requiring scratch until constructed. Guessing helper values, or declaring the fields kernel-owned, would not satisfy the unchanged UAPI.

boundaries.question: Whether the hardware has a second interpolation, derivative or blend mode that Metal never emits.
boundaries.why_out_of_scope_for_now: EXP-0111 FS-05 states the general form of this boundary precisely: 'no MSL-level probe can distinguish "the hardware has only one mode" from "the hardware has a second mode Metal simply never emits" - there is no compiler-reachable starting point to perturb', and an unmotivated blind bit sweep 'would be closer to random fault-hunting than a falsifiable test'.
boundaries.consequence_for_the_driver: This is a bounded UNKNOWN, not a missing measurement. The Rosenzweig extrapolate-and-test method still applies wherever a MOTIVATED hypothesis exists - EXP-0147 found matrix multiply-subtract exactly that way - but it needs a hypothesis, not a sweep.
boundaries.note: The inert-field sweeps (EXP-0163, EXP-0172) are the partial answer: they turn 'Metal always emits this value' into a measured don't-care envelope, which is the strongest statement available without a hypothesis.

boundaries.question: Apple's inlining heuristic - why a fragment epilog is inlined while a vertex fetch helper is kept out of line.
boundaries.why_out_of_scope: EXP-0137 declared it out of scope in its own pre-registration: 'it is not a hardware fact and a driver's own backend controls its own out-of-lining unconditionally regardless of what Apple's compiler happens to choose.' Answering it would mean studying Apple's compiler.
boundaries.consequence_for_the_driver: None. The driver picks its own out-of-lining policy.
